raw_case_text:
A 58-year-old Thai previously healthy male farmer, living in Roi Et Province (Northeast Thailand), was referred to our hospital, King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital, due to problems with total ophthalmoparesis and productive cough for 2 months. Two months prior to admission (PTA), he developed productive cough and low-grade fever with no response to many courses of antibiotic treatment. One month PTA, he noted binocular horizontal diplopia of the right eye, before progression to visual loss and ptosis despite antibiotic and steroid treatment. His past medical history was unremarkable except heavy alcoholic drinking.
The right eye examination revealed eyelid swelling, proptosis, marked chemosis, and complete ptosis; light perception of visual acuity; absent afferent pupillary reflex; and optic disk swelling and retinal hemorrhage. Neurological examination revealed right eye total ophthalmoparesis and decreased pinprick sensation of right cranial VI nerve area. Multiple dental caries were noted. Pulmonary examination revealed fine crackles at both the lungs. Other examination was unremarkable.
Complete blood count showed hemoglobin of 9.3 g/dL, white blood cells of 25,540 cells/mm3 (85.1% neutrophil, 9.8% lymphocyte, and 4.8% monocyte), and platelets of 697,000 cells/mm3. Blood chemistry was normal. Anti-HIV test was negative. Chest X-ray revealed bilateral diffuse reticulonodular and alveolar infiltrations. Orbital computed tomography revealed a 1.5 x 2.9 x 1.5 cm rim-enhancing hypodense lesion at the right orbital apex abutting to the optic nerve sheath complex and right medial rectus muscle (Figure 1).
A diagnosis of orbital and pulmonary infections was made, and emergent anterior orbitotomy was performed and revealed purulent discharge from the orbit. The pus and sputum Gram stain exhibited many Gram-positive filamentous bacilli, but non-acid-fast, on both standard and modified acid-fast bacilli stains. Hence, Actinomyces species was suspected, and Nocardia species could be excluded due to negative results on modified AFB stain. The pus cultures finally grew Actinomyces israelii (Figures 2(a) and 2(b)). Further bacterial identification by base sequencing of 16S ribosomal DNA was A. israelii with 99% identity (NCBI BLAST Search).
He was given penicillin G sodium of 24 million units per day for 6 weeks and amoxicillin of 2 g per day for another 12 months. After 10 days of treatment, there was a much improvement of lung infiltrates on his chest X-ray. The patient was doing well when last seen 1 year after discharge with mild residual impaired ophthalmoparesis and ptosis but still moderate visual impairment.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 58-year-old Thai male farmer presented with a 2-month history of productive cough and low-grade fever, and a 1-month history of right-sided diplopia progressing to complete right visual loss, ptosis, and total ophthalmoparesis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two months prior to admission, the patient developed a productive cough and low-grade fever unresponsive to multiple courses of outpatient antibiotics. One month prior to admission, he developed binocular horizontal diplopia of the right eye that progressed to complete ptosis, proptosis, total ophthalmoparesis, and visual loss despite antibiotic and corticosteroid therapy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy Thai male farmer from Roi Et Province (Northeast Thailand) with a history of heavy alcohol consumption.

objective.physical_examination: Right eye exam revealed eyelid swelling, proptosis, marked conjunctival chemosis, complete ptosis, visual acuity reduced to light perception, absent afferent pupillary defect (RAPD), optic disc swelling, retinal hemorrhage, total external ophthalmoparesis, and decreased pinprick sensation in the right cranial nerve V1 distribution. Oral exam showed multiple dental caries, and chest auscultation revealed bilateral fine crackles.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC showed anemia (Hb 9.3 g/dL), marked leukocytosis (WBC 25,540 cells/mm3; 85.1% neutrophils, 9.8% lymphocytes, 4.8% monocytes), and thrombocytosis (platelets 697,000 cells/mm3). Blood chemistry was normal and anti-HIV serology was negative. Chest X-ray demonstrated bilateral diffuse reticulonodular and alveolar infiltrates.
objective.advanced_workup: Orbital CT revealed a 1.5 x 2.9 x 1.5 cm rim-enhancing hypodense abscess at the right orbital apex abutting the optic nerve sheath complex and right medial rectus muscle. Emergent anterior orbitotomy drained purulent material; Gram stain of both orbital pus and sputum showed abundant Gram-positive filamentous bacilli that were negative on both standard and modified acid-fast stains.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Disseminated pulmonary and right orbital apex actinomycosis caused by Actinomyces israelii (with Nocardia species excluded by negative modified AFB staining) was confirmed via orbital pus culture and 16S rDNA sequencing (99% identity to A. israelii by NCBI BLAST). Following emergent anterior orbitotomy drainage, he was treated with intravenous penicillin G sodium (24 million units/day for 6 weeks) followed by oral amoxicillin (2 g/day for 12 months), resulting in rapid pulmonary radiographic clearing within 10 days and sustained systemic cure at 1-year follow-up with mild residual right ptosis/ophthalmoparesis and moderate visual impairment.
